title: Which sign goes in each box, with more floors?
description: Six pairs of numbers are compared on a longer floor line, with floors far above and far below the ground. The floor lying higher is the greater number, and one pair is checked by counting floors down.
teaching_notes: One idea: the floor that lies higher is the greater number, however far the line goes. Watch for students who think a bigger digit below the ground is a greater number.

video_script.why: The child compares numbers beyond the printed floors by imagining the line continuing up and down.
video_script.substitution: the book's own six pairs of numbers on an imagined taller block
video_script.anchor: the longer floor line of Ruhee, with six pairs of numbers to compare
video_script.payoff_line: Whichever floor lies higher is the greater number.

final_answer.spoken: greater than, greater than, greater than, greater than, less than and greater than

names.Ruhee: the multi-storey block of floors above and below the ground, used as the model for integers

hold_back: Answer: a. >, b. >, c. >, d. >, e. <, f. >
never_show: a bigger digit read as a greater number below the ground
maths_rules: −10 > −12 (twelve floors down is lower than ten floors down).
+17 > −10; +9 > −9; +15 > −17 (above the ground is higher than below it).
−25 < −7 (twenty five floors down is lower than seven floors down).
video_script.design: One idea: the higher floor is the greater number. One longer floor line throughout. Method as in the solved examples.

beats.on_screen: title card More Floors; the floor line of the tall block grows taller above and deeper below, with six pairs of numbers and an empty box in each

marks.scene: the title card arrives and the floor line appears
marks.more: the line grows taller above and deeper below the ground
marks.ask: the six pairs and the question are written into the anchor band

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about the floors of Ruhee.
<bookmark mark='more'/>Imagine the block with many more floors above and below the ground.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which sign goes in each of the six boxes, less than or greater than?

beats.on_screen: the six pairs stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board while the child thinks

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the longer floor line with the ground at 0, plus floors above in teal and minus floors below in amber; a down arrow is tagged lower

marks.line: the longer floor line is shown with the ground at the middle
marks.way: the solved example from the book is shown beside the line
marks.far: a down arrow is drawn along the amber floors

narration: <bookmark mark='line'/>More floors do not change the rule, because the floors are still on one line.
<bookmark mark='way'/>We solve it the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='far'/>The further down a floor lies, the lower it is.

marks.given: the line Given is written with the six pairs
marks.rest: the last three pairs are written under the first three

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, six pairs of numbers.
Minus ten and minus twelve, plus seventeen and minus ten, zero and minus twenty.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>Plus nine and minus nine, minus twenty five and minus seven, plus fifteen and minus seventeen.

beats.on_screen: To find: the sign, < or >, for each box

marks.find: the line To find is written under Given

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the sign for each box.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: −10 is 10 floors down and −12 is 12 floors down, so −10 > −12

marks.both: floors minus ten and minus twelve are lit below the ground
marks.sign: floor minus ten is outlined above floor minus twelve and the sign is filled

narration: <bookmark mark='both'/>Step one, minus ten and minus twelve are both below the ground.
Minus twelve is twelve floors down, which is further down than minus ten.
<bookmark mark='sign'/>The higher floor is minus ten, so minus ten is greater than minus twelve.

marks.deep: floor minus twenty five is lit far below floor minus seven and the sign is filled

narration: <bookmark mark='deep'/>Step two, minus twenty five lies far below minus seven.
The lower floor is the smaller number, so minus twenty five is less than minus seven.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: +17, +9 and +15 lie above the ground, −10, −9 and −17 lie below it: +17 > −10, +9 > −9, +15 > −17

marks.above: the three plus floors are lit above the ground
marks.below: the three minus floors are lit below the ground and the signs are filled

narration: <bookmark mark='above'/>Step three, plus seventeen, plus nine and plus fifteen lie above the ground.
<bookmark mark='below'/>Minus ten, minus nine and minus seventeen lie below it, so each plus floor is greater.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: 0 is the ground floor, above −20, so 0 > −20

marks.zero: the ground floor is outlined above floor minus twenty and the sign is filled

narration: <bookmark mark='zero'/>Step four, zero is the ground floor.
Minus twenty lies far below it, so zero is greater than minus twenty.

beats.on_screen: Step 5: check the first pair, count floors down from 0: 10 floors down is higher than 12 floors down

marks.check: the lift counts down from the ground floor
marks.ok: floors minus ten and minus twelve are lit and the sign is ticked

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step five, check the first pair by counting floors down from zero.
<bookmark mark='ok'/>Ten floors down is higher than twelve floors down, which agrees with greater than.

beats.on_screen: Answer: a. >, b. >, c. >, d. >, e. <, f. >

marks.ans: the answer line is boxed on the working board
marks.pay: the higher floor of each pair is outlined

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The signs are greater than, greater than, greater than, greater than, less than and greater than.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>Whichever floor lies higher is the greater number.
